utterances.text: So in relation to zone 1, is that the reference that -- that you make to the -- to the zone as indicated on the -- on the map?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. Zone 1 is the area where the hospital is placed, and this area where still are Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, I would like to turn to tab 39 for a moment but keep that page open. Now, tab 39, the registry have got all the details in relation to it, but I will call it out. It is 04247566 through to 7567, and the B/C/S is 04247566 through to 67 also. Have you got that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's a medical report from Vukovar. If we look at the second page, the 567 page, we see Jan Schou; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So who compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I -- I compiled it in Belgrade on the evening on the 18th, together with an -- some staff from the ECMM, and send it to -- to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we'll -- we have seen the reference to the other document, the town hospital, town hall are situated in zone 1. Could you please just refer to the second page of your personal report, 3, which is comments.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: My comments is that "JNA do not know the exact position of the hospital. They were firing -- they fired at town hall, which is the hospital."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was from the hill where we were -- what is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I seem to have some form of interference coming in being from outside. It is still continuing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now it's gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So going back to the original document, and I will come on to your medical report in a moment. We've got the town hospital and the town hall are situated in zone 1. 4, they stated that a meeting was going on between the JNA and Croatian forces at the bus station.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You've got that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What was that meeting about? Are you able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I -- we were only told that it was about the -- the surrender of the Croatian force, because they were only -- we were told that they were only 200 Croatians -- forces back in zone 1 and about 60 in zone 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, let's go to C: "We visited the town." Could you tell us please about this entry?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We visited the town, yes, we went to that point, that hill in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: And were looking out over the bus station to the region 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And as I say, you have told us about the refugee location at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can I deal with Velepromet when we're dealing with it? We have an entry here that they had to stay. Can you remember if there was any JNA officer who was present with you at that time or JNA representative?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that Major Sljivancanin was at that -- he was together with us on the whole visit to Vukovar. And I also had take a picture of him at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And if there is any dispute about it, can I just ask for clarification, please, it will be our tab 41, and the number is 0036-6979. It's a 65 ter number 66. Can we produce that? No, it's 66979. Can we move on? That's 73. There we are.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that's, I think, a photograph that you actually took of Major Sljivancanin on the 18th at the Velepromet facility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. Can we just see, when we look at the photograph, I don't know if it comes on the computer, yes, it does, we're looking down from -- from the road itself. What do we see down at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We see the refugees at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Those are the refugees that you had spoken to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. We'll just leave that. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I wonder perhaps if the wisest course would be for all the photographs to go in as one exhibit, because they tend to come from this witness and rather than deal with anything specifically, it might just be easier if they go in as a bunch of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have two in already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, and they're the same source. For my part, I would be quite happy for them to go in as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be added to the previous exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's very kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, may I deal then, please, with entry 4 of this handwritten document? "We spoke to." Now, we have got three names. I want to deal b and c, if I may. There we have Major Sljivancanin, Veselin. Where did the information that he was the commander of the group south come from?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I am sure you will remember, Your Honours, this document was discussed with the previous witness. And I think that was the way Mr. Moore asked the question, that he was on behalf of Operations Group South, and I think that's what the document itself indicates. I think that was the wording, that was the reason we didn't discuss the document much because it was being defined as being on behalf of Operations Group South, and that was how it was recorded in Mr. Kypr's diary, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful to my learned friend for giving evidence. All I'm doing is asking this witness does he know where this came from. That's all I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I then ask you, please, to return to tab 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, might I make application to enter tab 23 as an exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 339, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now can I just deal, please, with this particular document. You've told us already that you compiled this document yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can you please -- we'll deal with it systematically, if we may, just work our way down. So number 1, we see it's the 18th of November, medical report from Vukovar. What does the first paragraph deal with, please? Perhaps if you will read it out and then explain the first part.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. It is what -- this medical report is what -- what we have to stabilised before we can make an evacuation of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when we have the entry: "JNA demand CNG to lay down weapons before evacuation." Who -- who -- well, you clearly wrote it. But whose idea was it? Is it your suggestion or --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, it's -- no, we were told that from her, I'm not sure which person, but one of the officers from JNA, that -- that -- that CNG had to lay down their weapons before we could start an evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then there is: "No cease-fire for today." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'd like to deal with the -- the third entry, if I may, starting "The chain of command." Would you be kind enough to read that out, please, and then tell us what exactly it means?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It means -- "The chain of command in JNA from top to bottom must know all details of evacuation (agreements)." And that means that even that -- the day, when we -- the same day, the 18th, when we tried to reach the area we were stopped by a check-point outside Sid. And they did not know that we were arrived. Even if the liaison officer said that that was an agreement and we have a paper from the general, but the -- the check-point did not know it. So all the people down in the JNA army did not know what's -- what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So in relation to this entry, is it a proposal or --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It is a -- it is a statement that we had -- that before we could evacuate the people, all the people on every layer had to know that we were going to evacuate that people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And here it is in your document, but was there any arrangement for the JNA soldiers at various levels to be informed of this requirement? There is a difference between writing something down in a personal note with an intention, and whether the intention manifests itself, whether it comes into being. So can you tell us then, please, whether this occurred or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I can only tell you that before we start an evacuation we would try to make sure that every person knows that we are going to evacuate the -- the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: This document was compiled where?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: By you on what date?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: By me on the 18th of November in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when you compiled the document and your proposals, did you communicate that, did you tell anybody about what you thought was necessary, as a doctor, for the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. If you mean what -- what I have to use of equipment, no, I have not seen the hospital. I did not know exactly how many people there were in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I only had these, you can say, base -- this things to be established before -- before we get to the hospital so we could reach the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, you are using the phrase "to things to be established." So here you are as a doctor, you are there with a specific brief as a doctor, and you are saying concerning the evacuation of the hospital, did you tell anybody, Well, I think this is what needs to be done?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, we told -- told Zagreb, our headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. So who told Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I told Zagreb with this, I sent this report, medical report back to Zagreb, to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when did you do that, when you returned to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: When I returned to Belgrade on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, can I just move on, about the -- the brackets, if I keep it simple, "agreements." Do you see that your entry, it's in your handwriting, "agreements." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I mean agreement from -- I mean that the -- the people involved, the JNA and -- and the Croats, that they are agreed with -- that we are coming and that we are evacuate the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's just carry on. Number 4, we can see that there is the level of destruction is referred to; I won't go into that. 5, there is a reference to from the south you must bypass all JNA forces. What is meant by that, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That -- that meant that if we had to take the wounded out of the hospital from south, then it must be through the city, through all the JNA or the paramilitarian forces. So we have to travelling through the forces with the wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what was the conclusions that you recommended?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: My recommend was that we had to take the wounded out of the city by north or by the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's look at entry 2, please. "Refugees and wounded in JNA-controlled area." What was your finding there, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Wait a minute, where -- okay, there it is. Can you explain it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have -- we've got number 1 with some headings and then number 2 we've got headings in your handwriting. And I want to deal with number 2. I think you see it on the page you have?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Refugees and wounded in JNA-controlled area."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then you have the various what I call sub-paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could you just read it out, and we'll deal with them one by one. Would you mind?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. Because of the -- it was made, you can say, as a conclusion of the refugees centre. Where -- with no registration of the people, we saw no medical supply. There were no made medical staff at all at that refugee centre. And they cannot move as they want. It was what I told you before, that they were -- the JNA said that they could go but they said -- when we asked them, we are not allowed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I just deal with one little comment that you have made there? You saw no medical supply, and there was no medical staff at all at the refugee centre. Was there necessary for there to be medical supply or medical staff present at the Velepromet facility within your professional judgement?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Because it was civilian from the city, and some of them were, you can say, lightly wounded. They were not laying down, but they were lightly wounded, and of course they have to be treated by doctors, or medical staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's carry on, please. The fourth entry: "They have not food enough." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And who is "they" and where is that location?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It's the refugee centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then number 5, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Number 5, that they have no -- there is no -- no heating in that building, they said. I was not in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think the entry says: "They have no means for heating except cooking." So what did you find personally, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I only remember that of course -- they have a place where they could cook, could make their food, this small food they have. But there were no heating at all in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And how cold was it?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was in November, so it was sometimes -- we were freezing and we have dry clothes every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn over the page, if I may, please. Could you read out this, all of it, please, this subentry?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "Some family members are taken away. (Prisoners" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think it just says "prison," doesn't it question mark?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So: "Some family members are taken away, prison?" What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That mean that when we talk with some of the refugees, they said that some of their family members were arrested or taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And taken away by whom?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: By the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any explanation ever given to you on the 18th of why it was certain people were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then we've got "conclusion." I presume that this is the International --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- Committee for the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Should take over immediately." Why did you make that particular conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: So they could -- because it's their -- it's normally their job to register, to divide help for refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: How important in your judgement was it that the ICRC should take over the situation as you found it?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I found it important. That's why I have the conclusion. Because we have no -- we are only monitors so we have no equipment at all to help. So there must be an international health organisation, the ICRC or Medecins sans Frontieres or something like that, to take over the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. We're nearly finished. We've come to the comment box. I've already dealt with the JNA firing at the town hall which actually was the hospital. Can we go to the second subheading starting "no political speaking officers."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. This especially is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could you read it out into the? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No political speaking officers involving" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Involved"?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "Involved. They are only talking politics matter and delay the whole who process."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let me just see it. Perhaps my eyesight is a little better. "No political speaking officers involved. They only talk political matters and delay the whole process." Now, can we deal, please, with delaying the whole process? What did you mean by that entry?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I mean that the whole day, when we tried to do something, walk -- talk with some of the refugees or something, we were almost delayed the whole time of Major Sljivancanin. And that's -- that's -- I could have write his name. Instead of saying "political speaking officers," I mean Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And how long did he stay with you that day? Try and give us an impression, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: He was with us the whole -- I think the whole day until we left Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "delay"? How was that -- how did that happen?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: By I mean delay, it means that he -- every time we try to ask for something or ask something for the refugees or something, he start with, you can say, a political speech about Croatian and about the Ustasha and about all this. So -- so every time he start, he start with kind of political speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But you say "and all this." Please understand we need to hear, as best you can remember, what sort of things Major Sljivancanin was saying. Just try and give us a tone or texture.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I think it's -- I think it's difficult. It's just that they -- that these people, that they are fighting against in the city, they are Ustasha, and they are not normal soldiers, and they -- yes. What can I say more? It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let us then carry on, if I may. You've told us that you were -- from the documents we can see it's 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, may I make that document an exhibit, if I have not done so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 340.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I will return to the original tab 23, just for completeness sake. You have got the briefing in Velepromet, 1430 to 1445; talking to refugees, 1445 to 1530; and then departure, Vukovar, 1530; and arrival at the hotel, presumably in Zagreb. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, this is in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, that's not in Zagreb. That's in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You're quite right, it's my fault. Thank you. Can I deal then, please, with the 19th of November? The following day. Now, that is a day that you clearly were involved in. Can you remember approximately what time you left?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We left Belgrade in the morning. I'm not sure of the time. 8.00 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And can you tell us then where you went?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We went to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what happened at Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: At Negoslavci we have a meeting in the military headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We were told that they had -- that the JNA had taken over the hospital or the whole area, and we were told that -- and -- I'm not sure it was in the morning or later that day, we were told that some of the staff, Dr. Bosanac and some of the staff and some of the people from the hospital were taken away. And the JNA told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did they give any explanation why it was --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was because they were criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you remember if there was any reference about other people being taken away?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, not -- no, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So in relation to the briefing, did you actually go to the hospital itself or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: On the 19th, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We have it -- a contact with Dr. Bosanac, with mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's just deal with that, please. You say that you spoke to Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I did not myself. It was -- I think it was Mr. Kypr that spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. When you spoke to Dr. Bosanac, can you remember in general terms what was said or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. She said that terrible things were going on, and we -- we had to -- we had to come to the hospital immediately, and then the connection was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And was there anything that was -- was said about speaking to Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only that terrible things happened in the hospital. That's what I -- what I heard, not what I heard, what Mr. Kypr that she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Were you able, or did you tell anybody from the JNA that you had made a phone call to Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. We -- I'm not sure which person we said it to, but we said that we have contact with the -- with Dr. Bosanac and that we want to go to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I know that Major Sljivancanin at -- at that time or maybe just an hour later or something said that we are not allowed to go to the hospital due to -- they were still fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: This was on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what about the phone call to Dr. Bosanac? Were you able or allowed to phone her again?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. We were told that we were not allowed to phone her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And can you remember who it was who said that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did he indicate why it was that you weren't able to speak to Sljivancanin -- why you weren't able to speak to Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Because -- because she were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did he say anything else about her?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only this: That she were criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: With regard to the hospital itself, was it important that you go to the hospital that day or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was important because we -- we want to -- monitoring the evacuation of the hospital, and monitoring will of course start when -- when the hospital is taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: How important is it, if you are going to have an evacuation of wounded or perhaps even non-wounded people, that you find out the level of injury or the numbers that have to be transported? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, not -- no. You have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: -- rearrange.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You've got an evacuation to make --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- of a hospital. Hospitals can have different types of injuries?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If you are wanting to have a successful evacuation, how important is it to know what medical requirements there are to take the injured people away?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It is, of course, important to know how many people there are, how seriously injured they are. But you know the -- the evacuation itself, it must come from JNA or Red Cross or another. Because we have no equipment in the monitoring mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But in relation to the evacuation, was it important or not to find out the level of injuries that -- and the numbers --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, it was important to know how many people it -- there were at the hospital we had to evacuate. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you able to -- or did you have any accurate indication of the numbers that you would be evacuating or not on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I have no number at the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we deal then with the 19th, what happened then at that time. Did you have any other discussions with Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: There was a discussion in the evening, but I cannot refer it, I cannot remember what it's about. It's just that we will receive some message from -- about the evacuation, and the -- some of the team went back to Belgrade that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What about you? Where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I stay in Negoslavci that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And who did you stay in Negoslavci with? Was there any other monitor?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: There was -- I'm not sure that it was Mr. Kypr or -- but there were -- I was together with some other monitors; I was not alone. We were -- we had a -- a vehicle there, so we must at least be three people; a driver and two monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you make any further request to go to see the hospital, further request on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: On the 19th, yes. In the evening we tried to -- to -- we ask if we could go to -- to the hospital, but they -- we could not go because they are still fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is it a case of you saying there was fighting, or is it a case that you were told that there was fighting?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We were told that they were fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's then move to the following day, the 20th. Now, can you remember the morning of the 20th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I can remember the morning in that way that there was an agreement from -- made -- I think made in Zagreb that Mr. Kypr and I were allowed to go to the hospital to -- to monitoring the evacuation which Red Cross should be -- no, not -- no, no. Which JNA should take -- should evacuate. The JNA should evacuate the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let's just -- you say you remember in the morning that there was an agreement, you think, made in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That you were allowed to go to the hospital. And you have said to monitor the evacuation. But who was to be responsible for the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: The JNA was responsible for the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what part was the ICRC to play?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: They have to make register about all the patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did you know from your own personal knowledge when it was the ICRC were supposed to register the patients? Now, if you don't know, don't guess, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you ever see the document, what I will call the evacuation document, prior to going to the hospital on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So let's deal then, please, with the 20th. You say that you set off. So let's deal with the morning, please. What -- what is your first memory on the -- on the morning of the 20th? Can you tell the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. We have a short briefing in Negoslavci, and at that time the monitor -- the other monitor arrived from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: And then I was told that it was only me and Mr. Kypr that were -- that should monitoring the hospital. And then we went from Negoslavci in the morning at 8.00, I think it was, to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And as far as you understood it, on the morning of the 20th --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: The morning of the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. What time did you believe that you would be going to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We thought we should go to the hospital immediately, at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And were you able to get to the hospital at 8.00?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. We were stopped at the bridge in -- in the middle of the city. And we were stopped because there was an APC on the bridge, and Major Sljivancanin was at that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation or did you hear any explanation given by Major Sljivancanin about why you couldn't proceed?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: He said that we couldn't proceed because the road was not clear; there were snipers and there was still some fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, because we saw no fighting. We only saw shooting in the area, so -- celebrating the victory. And we saw some vehicles driving on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's the hearing. If you look at the transcript at line 18, do you see it on the left-hand side, 64, 18? No, on the screen. Have you got the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Does it have a transcript?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It is in Serbo-Croatian, I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is there one in English there? I hope so.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, we saw no fire -- there were no fighting in the area. There were only celebrating and firing in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In the air, because it comes across "in the area."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In the air.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: In the air, just firing, celebrating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let us deal with the bridge. I will show you a video perhaps of that in a moment. But at the time you've said you were rather surprised. How long did you remain at the bridge, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did you, when I say "you" I mean not just you but a group, did you as a group or individually protest about the blockage on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And who did you protest to?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: To Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And can you remember what he said, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Just that he would not let us allowed to go to the other side because due to our security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I deal, please, with your stopping on the bridge and the situation that was around you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you see any other military forces around you at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, at the bridge we were secure by the military police. They have a car and there were some maybe military police from JNA. And then around us, especially on the stairs, up to a bank, a civilian bank just beneath, there were a lot of Chetniks sitting or -- you can call it. They wore civilian clothes and some military clothes and some -- and they were shooting in the air, and they were shouting and they were drinking, and there were women also with guns and shooting and drinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, you have said the word "area," but by your own -- it says "in the air." All right. And how did you find the atmosphere at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was -- oh, have to find the word. There were accusative to the EC members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now I want you to look at a video which we have seen, which is about to be played. I'm told if you could close down your microphone. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I don't know about others, but I can't hear any sound again, and I have checked three times whether there was going to be a sound, and I was told on three occasions that there was sound. So I don't know whether -- why there is a problem because I have checked literally so many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we please go back to the beginning and have the sound? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Have you seen that video before?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that video before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. And with regard to the incident itself, is it right that you saw that incident obviously not that close but --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I saw it, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Was that the only argument that there was on the bridge with Sljivancanin or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Was that the only argument, the only disagreement with Major Sljivancanin on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. The man from the Red Cross had a -- and shouting with Major Sljivancanin the evening before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll come back to that. But if I just deal with the bridge, did you see any other arguments with Sljivancanin or not? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No, there wasn't; or no, you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us that in actual fact you'd seen an argument previously with that gentleman who is called Nicholas Borsinger. Now, where had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I seen him in the headquarter in Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And in what circumstances had you seen him?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I think it was at the meeting the evening before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you say that you saw him having an argument with Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what -- what occurred?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It occurred about he -- he want to go to the hospital, the evening before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when he said that, did Major Sljivancanin make any reply?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only that he could not go to the hospital because there were -- they were fighting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you remember why the -- why Borsinger, or the ICRC representative -- why Borsinger wanted to go to the hospital the previous evening?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. He only -- the only thing I know is he want to make registration of the patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I deal, then, with the bridge? You've told us about the argument and the disagreement itself. You had Mr. Kypr with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But you did not have Colonel Cunningham with you that day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Where was Cunningham on the 20th, at around about 10.00? I'm not asking that you know exactly, just in general.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, he is I think, back in Belgrade to arrange the further evacuation when we left the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I want to deal, before we move over the bridge, I want to deal with the relationship between Cunningham and Nicholas Borsinger. I'd like you, if you would be kind enough, please, to turn up tab 27. This, I believe, is Exhibit 333. Now, I don't want to go in any great detail about other -- other parts of this. I have no doubt at all that you'll be asked lots of questions about it. But I want to deal just with the second paragraph. Well, perhaps the better one to deal with is if you go to page ZA00-4267, do you see that, the top of the page? 4267, have you got that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Have you got tab 27?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: 27, no. I have 26. And 27, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you go to 27, open it up, and if you look at the top of the page you will have various numbers, which is ZA00-4267. Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It should be a typed document.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, 4267. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we just look at the very bottom of that page. It is subparagraph number 7. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "ICRC leader behaviour-Vukovar evacuation."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If I put it in very round terms, would it be right to say that there was not -- in the English phrase, not a lot of love lost between Colonel Cunningham and Mr. Borsinger?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the background, was there a reason that there seemed to have been an element of disagreement between both of them?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that there was -- there were -- they should have taken a meeting on the other side of Vukovar -- other side of the Dunav some days before where the IC [sic] member left the Red Cross in the middle of nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, you have said the IC. Do you mean the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: The ECMM, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So can we just deal with this, please? So some days before, the ECMM member, is that Colonel Cunningham or ...

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's Colonel Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So Colonel Cunningham left the Red Cross. Was that Mr. Borsinger or left the Red Cross generally?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Left them -- what do you mean "left them"? He just said, Out of the car and stay there, or was there a meeting? Can you be a little more precise?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I have just heard it from Borsinger who claimed that Cunningham, that he had to walk, I think, 10 kilometres back to a town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. So there was a meeting and --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It's -- it's only -- I only heard a little about it, but I know there was some disagreement between these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. And so with regard to the references to the ICRC leader by Cunningham, are you able to assess whether Cunningham, putting it as politely as I can, was not a great fan of Nicholas Borsinger, and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. If we just put that document away for a moment. We are at the bridge, and eventually, as we see, the APC is removed. And you made your way to the hospital. When you were in the queue, were you aware that a number of buses had crossed over the Vukovar river on the other bridge with a large number of principally men under the control of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We were not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: When you got to the hospital, how did you find the overall situation?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I found the overall situation very bad. The -- we were -- we were told, and we saw, that the -- that a military medical unit had taken over the hospital. And in the hospital there were these medical people, and there were a lot of -- we can call them Chetniks inside the hospital, and there were guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the Chetniks who were inside the hospital, were you able to work out if any of them had taken some alcoholic drinks?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, they were drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: And also -- also some of these from the medical staff, they were also -- they look -- I'm not sure that they have drunk, but they look like they have drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what about the level of organisation by the JNA medical staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: At that time there were no organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The patients that you had gone to collect, were they still in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: In the hospital there were most -- mostly women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: And there were no -- and there were no -- not no, but there were only few men in this -- in the basement of the hospital and there were no people wounded the last day. I think the sick and the wounded in the hospital, they were wounded almost 14 days before, I think. There were no wounded -- no -- no wounded from the -- from the last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No recent wounded. Is that how --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No recent wounded, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, you said that there were only a few men. Did it surprise you that there were only a few men?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yeah. It surprised us, and we asked why -- where the men were, and we were told that they were taken away and some of them were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, when you said you asked, who did you ask and who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: All our information came from Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when Major Sljivancanin told you that, did you inquire why it was that they had been taken away?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only that -- the same as yes, they were criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to find out, what exactly it was he said. So he said what, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I can only remember that he said that they were -- they were criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did he say where they were taken to?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Only to what?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: To a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: To a prison. Did he say where that prison was?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of the civilians who were present at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we speak to some -- some patient, and some of them told us that the men or some of the men were taken away during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And, again, did you make any inquiry why it was that men were taken away during the night?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We -- yes, we said that due to the -- due to the agreement, we should evacuate all wounded from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And was there any reply to that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Only that they -- that they were prisoner of war. Or criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: How often did you see Sljivancanin that day?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I saw him when we arrived to the hospital and he -- I think he were one hour or something like that, and then I don't remember -- I know that he -- there was time when he -- he was not present at the hospital, but I can't say how long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like you just to -- and I don't mean this in any discourteous way, please understand that, there you are, you get to the hospital, you leave across the bridge, you said you got there about 8.00, two hours, 10.00, how long did it take you to get to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: From the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. And when was it that you left the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: We left the hospital in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you -- you say that you had spoken to Sljivancanin at the hospital. Can you give us an indication of when it was --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: When we arrived the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, please listen. When it was that he was not there?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, was it in the afternoon or in the morning? Can you help us in the generality?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: He was when we arrived to the hospital, I can't tell you more. I can't tell you any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You don't know when he left?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: When in actual fact you departed from the hospital, in the convoy --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- was he there or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's deal, then, with the evacuation of the hospital with the JNA medical officers. How well was that done at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Very bad. There were no organisation at the hospital at the 20th of November. And it was a few person from the old staff that loaded the -- the sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'd like to -- you to look at a video, please, and I hope that the sound again will be on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what is the exhibit number of this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We're just locating it. It's on the index. It's Exhibit 319. Your Honour will find it on the final page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Again, have you seen that video before?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I have seen that video, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think you saw it here?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And there is Borsinger saying that the ICRC were unable to do their job.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that, in your judgement, correct or not?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: They were told just outside -- outside -- when we entered the hospital the security of the hospital, if there were any security, were told that they -- the only person that could cross -- go to the hospital were Mr. Kypr and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You've told us that you saw Major Sljivancanin on the morning of the 20th, and you have said that he had had dealings with Borsinger on the bridge on the 20th, and Borsinger on the evening of the 19th.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did Major Sljivancanin ever express any view about the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Any opinion?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. He said to us, I can't remember if -- if it were in the morning or in the evening, he said it, but he said that he don't trust Red Cross, that they had tried to reach the hospital, but he had throw them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: He had what?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: He had take them back again. So that they couldn't reach the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And to what day did that refer?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That referred to the 19th in the evening, or in the night between the 19th and the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did he say why he didn't trust the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I deal with, again, Major Sljivancanin at the hospital? You have told us that he was there in the morning of the 20th. Did you ever see any journalists at the hospital on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you saw the journalists? I'm not saying the exact time.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I -- I think it was in the afternoon or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: After -- after -- yes, 1.00, 2.00, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And was there any JNA representative with the journalists?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So Major Sljivancanin and the journalists. What was he doing with them at that time?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, did you see it?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I only saw that he bring some journalists in. I did not wait for the press conference or he -- whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The actual evacuation itself, can we just deal with that, I think, in brief order? But before we do, would you be kind enough, please, to deal with what I will call tab 40? It is not an exhibit as yet. The ERN number is 00099998 to 9999, both in English and B/C/S. Now, have you got this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is a typed document.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, if we just look at the second page, there seems to be a signature. It's in very -- a very bad photocopy, but just above it seems to be your name, Jan Schou, medical doctor, ECMM. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The date is the 22nd of the 11th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, who compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was this document -- why did you compile it? Why did you make it?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I make it in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And why did you do this document?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I do it as a report about the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital. And the report is giving to the head of mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. I'm not going to deal with the 19th. We've -- see that at the top. Then the 20th, there are various details. If we just look at the timing, 10.30, ECMM arrived at hospital, then there is the unloading. 1600 hours, it actually says "lived hospital." I presume that means left?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And "rest" stands for?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: The rest people in the hospital. The people we -- we left in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: In Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Then 1700 hours, bus with medical staff entered by Chetnik with -- with what?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: With knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Had you seen any misbehaviour, any bad behaviour by Chetniks in and around the hospital that day?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. I saw -- I saw some of these Chetniks beating the patient laying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And where was -- where were the patients? You say laying on the floor. Was that inside the hospital or --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It was inside the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And how many times did you see beatings or abuses?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Two or three times, I think. And then we -- we claim it to -- to the JNA -- to our security guard, and they -- they took the -- the people, the people outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if we look at 2100 hours, you arrived at the military infirmary in Sremska Mitrovica. I think is it right that one died en route and one, there was a immediate operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And we have got entries for 2200 and 2400 hours. And then we move on to the 21st of the 11th. And it relates to the Belgrade team, and the unloading of the wounded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I ask you just about the entry of -- for 900, the 40 badly wounded. What treatment was organised by the JNA for those badly wounded people?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: As I remember, there were no treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, but if my learned friend could just please slow down. We have an interpreter on the brink of collapse again. I believe it is very difficult for the accused, first and foremost, to follow the proceedings. Therefore, if my learned friend could just slow down slightly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Of course I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You have told us that there was -- let me just repeat that. I asked the question, what treatment was organised by the JNA for those badly wounded, and as you remember, there was no treatment. Can we look at the entry for 1500 hours, please? Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'm working on the basis that it's 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: 1500 hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Because 00, 1500 hours, then it goes on 1860, I'm working on the basis 1500 hours. And then: "Left behind 50 wounded SRB and 30 staff, SRB." Presumably that's Serb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And: "Plus two dying wounded Croat."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There is an entry just immediately below that, you see it says: "ICRC have the name of all wounded from the 21st of November."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, I stress the word "all". Did the ICRC have a list of all the wounded before that date?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. They only have the -- they only make list on the 21, 21st of November. And they have the list of all the wounded that were transported -- that were taking out of the hospital at the 21st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Just comments, if I may. We've already dealt with the 19th evidentially, but I'll deal with it here. Please just look at where comments is. Thank you. "ICMM doctor were not allowed to go to the hospital." The doctor, is that you?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And: "Told by JNA removed Ustasha wounded 8 plus 2 staff. ICMM" -- well --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No, that's -- the ICMM, that's the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. So told by JNA that they removed Ustasha wounded. There were 8 --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- and two staff?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Two from the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Who told you that on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any indication of either --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would really, really kindly ask my learned friend to please slow down a little and to make pauses between questions and answers. For the last five minutes I don't think the accused have been able to follow what exactly is going on here. The interpreters are having one hell of a time catching up. And if my learned friend could just slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, it's my fault. Normally I hear if the interpreters have a difficulty. I hear, Could counsel slow down. I've not heard anything like that. But I'll try to slow down, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal with the comments again, 19th of the 11th. "Told by JNA removed Ustasha wounded, 8 and 2 staff."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you said that was told by --

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Major --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'll pause. And was there any indication of where those wounded Ustasha were taken?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: To prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And with regard to the medical care, was there any reference to what would happen to them if they were -- because they were wounded?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's move to the 20th. There is reference to Chetnik in hospital. We've dealt with that. "Nothing prepared by JNA and ICRC." Well, we have heard about the ICRC and we have heard about the JNA; I needn't repeat that. Can we deal with A, please? "ICRC -- leader ICRC only criticised JNA."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. It was what I observed at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. "That he made no list of the wounded."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And that's of course because he was not allowed to go to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then 3: "Able to do nothing." Can we deal with,"JNA," please? Firstly, 1. Can you read it out, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. "No security. There were many Chetniks. Too many officers, only few soldier." It was the medical staff I mean there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And 3?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No control, no organising." In the hospital, of course. "Only few soldier helping carrying the wounded. Some Chetnik beat the wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that was in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: And that was in the hospital. And there was shooting in the area for fun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, it says "aria."

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: A musical note. But I take it that that's air?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: In the area. Around the hospital they were shooting, but it's celebrating again, for fun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. And 7, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: 7: "Mortar firing from the city." We heard a mortaring firing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then let's move on to the staff, what your conclusions were there.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "Most of the staff" -- it means the staff of the hospital, of the Vukovar Hospital. "The most of the staff went into the buses immediately." They did not help at all. "There were only two person from the staff, a priest and a nurse, that most of the time helped carrying and loaded the wounded." And: "There were no priority of the patient."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I mean that they just take the patient out of the hospital into these trucks, then one who can walk and then one on -- who were badly wounded, and then -- there were no priority. Normally you have one, two, three, four, priority, which kind of -- it's the kind of illness they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But why is priority important in an evacuation of wounded?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It's because they only have a few ambulance, and of course they have to put the badly wounded in the ambulance and the poor wounded in the buses, and not the opposite way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And even though it may seem perfectly obvious to you, why is that important?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It's because in -- in -- it is -- we saw it but it is really difficult to have badly wounded patient laying in a bus at the seat, over the seat. They are falling down and everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Just turning the page can we deal with 6, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No personnel in the ambulance." There were no medical personnel in the ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And again, why is that important?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Because they have to treat the wounded people on the transportation. Normally in a civilian ambulance there is two -- one or two person that could take care of this wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And why is it important to have the personnel? What affect can it have if you don't have it?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: If you don't have it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: On a long evacuation.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: On a long -- sometimes the patient may die because of he become -- became ill and couldn't breathe or something like that. You maybe had to help him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's deal with B, then, please, moving on.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No secure in transportation."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I mean there were no regular soldier that secured these transport of wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what -- what have we got just below that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "The Chetnik went into the buses and were treating the wounded with knives."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I presume they weren't treating them but perhaps threatening?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Threatening, okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And did you see that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: I did not see it. I heard it. I heard -- we were told that during this transportation to the military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then if we just look, if I do it shortly, I'll just take a pause for the translation. With regard to C and D, the infirmary in Sremska Mitrovica, what you're basically saying there is that it was good medical?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And there was food supply; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: There is reference to a pregnant woman dying and then one was sent to Belgrade for an operation?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let us deal then by way of comparison with the 21st of November. How did the ICRC perform the following day?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: The following day they -- there were at -- at the morning and member of the IC in the hospital, and he make lists of all the patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, shall I just read it into the record and hope that it doesn't offend anyone. 1, good prepared, list, et cetera; 2, good helping in organising all; and 3, the leader was only making trouble.

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. That's Mr. Borsinger, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Okay. B: "The lieutenant-colonel was making a good job." This is in respect of the JNA. "However, the buses were bad for wounded people." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What was 3 then, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: There was better security but still Chetnik in the hospital. It means that the hospital -- at the hospital there were more military police that day. So -- so no -- so there were a kind of guard around the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And number 4?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Number 4, 10 to 15 drunk officers, it was do nothing. And the drunk officers, from the medical unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And how badly drunk were they? Can you give us any indication of how you came to this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: They -- they must have walked like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Then moving on. "Staff" -- perhaps I needn't go on to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must stop you there, Mr. Moore. Our tapes are running out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I only have, I would think, about 20 minutes more, if that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now for the second break and resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. There is one thing that I would like to clarify. The exhibit marked as 338, we have the photographs that were at tab 41. It is a 65 ter document, number 66. The set contains 15 photographs. What I want to know is whether my learned friend has tendered all 15 photographs or just the ones that he's been showing the witness today. I believe that all 15 photographs from this tab number are actually in the folder, whereas my learned friend has only shown three. So that's one thing that I would like to clarify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer is so far there are only three photographs in the exhibit. If more are tendered by Mr. Moore, they can be included in that same exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And to help my learned friend, I will be referring to some of those photographs at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Dr. Schou, would you be kind enough, please, just to turn up - we've nearly finished - the document at our tab 40, which I will seek to make an exhibit in due course. Now we have finished at C, saying "staff." Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Good. So we have got staff, then ECMM?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Help carrying the first 10 wounded." Can you deal with number 2, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Number 2: "We were told we were not allowed to help. We were only allowed to monitoring."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And that it was JNA responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. And I see that -- Medecins sans Frontieres presumably is MSF, and there is reference to that. Now, may I just move down to general comments? Can we deal, please, with your assessment of the JNA participation?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes. I said with number 1 that they were "very bad organisation of the evacuation (logistic, organisation, work and their priority)".

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I deal with number 3?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No security of the wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that related to what, inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Outside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: It is inside the hospital and the transportation from Vukovar Hospital to the military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We've got 4 already. What about 5, please?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: "No control over Chetnik." It means that they could, at the 20th they could walk and -- walk inside the hospital. No one is stopping them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can I deal with number 6?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: Yes, number 6, that we were told that there were wounded and staff, some of the staff, they were removed from the hospital before we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And with regard to the wounded, as far as you are aware, did that -- an English word is "accord." Did that correspond, was that the same as the -- the agreement?

utterances.speaker: JAN SCHOU
utterances.text: No. The agreement said that we had to evacuate all the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
